# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` accesses the actual trained module through `view.model`, alongside `item_emb`, `log2feats`, `predict_score`, and public `user_train` histories. Loader batches contain `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` tensors shaped B × L.

`run_full_diagnosis` disables gradients, enters evaluation mode, and restores module modes and Python, NumPy, and Torch RNG states afterward.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding alignment:** Samples up to 2,048 item embeddings, excluding padding/reserved tokens. Reports `(mean pairwise cosine + 1)/2`; values near 1 indicate strong alignment, while approximately 0.5 means near-zero average cosine. This does not establish diversity or rank collapse.
- **Training margins:** Over ten batches, computes positive-minus-negative logits at finite, nonpadding positions. Reports mean, tenth percentile, fraction below zero, and fraction below 0.5. Larger margins and fewer ranking reversals generally indicate stronger sampled training separation; magnitudes depend on score scale.
- **Contract controls:** Checks left-padded readout, batch consistency, future-input invariance, dependency boundaries, normalization coupling, and synthetic boundary reachability. Export parity compares actual predictor scores/ranks when matching checkpoint weights are available.

Up to 32 deterministically selected users contribute two training prefixes each, scored against a target plus 99 unique negatives. Tests compare matched older/recent interior deletions, endpoint-preserving reorderings, and candidate-disjoint endpoint/interior replacements.

Paired changes measure target rank, target-minus-best-negative margin, and HR@10. Lower rank changes and higher margin/hit changes are favorable. Results average within users, then across users, with 10,000 user-bootstrap replicates and repeated/novel-target strata. Contract failures block sensitivity summaries.
